The GAN used is the authors' own 100-dimensional latent-space generator with a binary discriminator, not an SDV-family model. CTGAN is cited in related work as prior art, described as using mode-specific normalisation for mixed data types, but it is not run in the experiments.

The review applies a constraint-aware framework showing that protocol compliance and semantic preservation invalidate up to 80.3% of published adversarial examples under real-world conditions. CTGAN is cited among the GAN-based attack literature surveyed as an example of adversarial generative modeling relevant to intrusion detection evasion.

CTGAN is discussed in a dedicated subsection as a generative model that learns multi-modal tabular distributions and supports conditional sampling for synthetic data generation, but it is only described from cited literature, never implemented or run by the authors themselves.

It systematically compares CTGAN, a VAE, and an LLM as synthetic data generators across varying data-scarcity levels, finding CTGAN produces poor-fidelity, highly distinguishable samples while the VAE is most reliable. CTGAN (from the SDV family, with its Gaussian-mixture mode-specific normalization described and tuned via batch_size/generator_lr/discriminator_lr hyperparameters) is run as one of three generators benchmarked and ultimately rejected in favor of the VAE.

The survey describes and repeatedly discusses studies that use Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) for class-imbalance mitigation and synthetic attack-traffic generation in IDS datasets, but does not itself run any generator. CTGAN's conditional sampling and mode-specific normalization design is cited and its use in other authors' IDS pipelines is reviewed throughout, without SDV code being executed by this paper.

paper-jointly-trained-automation-explain.summary: This paper proposes JACK, a machine-learning framework developed with a construction company to estimate material requirements and generate project quotations from 207 construction projects, using cascaded and joint training with dropout layers and regression trees. To help clarify structural patterns for training, the authors used four algorithms from the SDV Python package—CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula—to generate synthetic training data, finding TVAE gave the lowest MAE. SDV's CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TVAE and GaussianCopula synthesizers were run directly via the library as data-augmentation generators feeding the downstream prediction model.

It is evaluated in a Synthetic Regulatory Sandbox, reporting large reductions in safety violation rates. The work's metadata lists a citation to the CTGAN paper, but no CTGAN/SDV-family mention or engagement appears anywhere in the retrieved full text.

paper-relational-context-learning-synthe.summary: This paper introduces RDB-PFN, a relational foundation model pre-trained purely on synthetic relational databases generated via a structural 'Relational Prior Generator', enabling in-context learning that generalizes to new database schemas without fine-tuning. It reports strong few-shot performance on 19 real-world relational prediction tasks using a lightweight Transformer over DFS-linearized inputs. SDV is cited in the related-work discussion as an early statistical-copula-based approach to relational data synthesis that the paper's diffusion-era and prior-based methods have since superseded.

paper-synthetic-blood-generation-fair-20.summary: This paper benchmarks seven generative models—CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula, CopulaGAN, MedGAN, DiscGAN, and FAST-ML—for synthesizing clinical blood test and demographic data across three medical datasets (an Irish hospital dataset, a UCI dataset, and the Korean NHIS 2002 dataset), evaluating them on statistical fidelity (KS, Wasserstein distance, JSD) and demographic fairness. It finds Gaussian Copula, TVAE, and CTGAN consistently achieve the best fidelity and least bias amplification, while MedGAN and DiscGAN degrade subgroup representation. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula and CopulaGAN synthesizers are run directly as four of the seven evaluated generative models and emerge as the top performers across all three datasets.

To test scalability, the authors extend their evaluation with CTGAN-generated synthetic network traffic traces to emulate networks of up to 100 nodes. CTGAN is used as an off-the-shelf generator to produce synthetic traces augmenting the empirical evaluation, not as the core contribution of the work.

The authors describe Deep-CTGAN as extending CTGAN's architecture by adding class-specific conditioning to the generator input, and also report a plain 'CTGAN' row as one of several augmentation baselines in their result tables. CTGAN's conditional generator design is the model the authors modify and extend into their proposed Deep-CTGAN, while a citation nominally attributed to the TGAN (2018) paper appears (likely mis-cited) in a sentence about SMOTE/ADASYN oversampling.

The metric is validated on production data from a German car manufacturer and on public fault-diagnosis benchmark data, and compared against rule-based approaches (ARM, CFDs) and other classifiers (SVMs, autoencoders). To further test scalability and computational performance, the authors synthetically expand both datasets to 100,000 records using CTGAN, treating it as a data-generation tool for a supplementary scalability evaluation rather than the paper's core contribution.

It is validated against 7 typical oversampling methods (including plain CTGAN, WGAN-GP, SNGAN, CGAN, ACGAN) on 12 real tabular datasets across F1 and AUC. CTGAN's conditional GAN architecture and mode-specific normalization are both the base the authors extend into their own generator and a baseline run head-to-head against it.

CTGAN, run as the default model from the SDV library with its conditional sampling capability, was evaluated as an augmentation generator but ultimately rejected in favor of SMOTENC after its synthetic feature distributions diverged more from the original data.

SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer is the generator that produces the coffee transaction data underlying the entire clustering study, with the original SDV (Patki et al. 2016) paper cited for how it records per-column distribution types.

CTGAN and TVAE, both introduced in the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are directly modified into new adversarial generator variants that anchor half of the paper's empirical comparison.

paper-fga-ids-federated-learning-2024.summary: This paper proposes FGA-IDS, a federated-learning-based intrusion detection system for UAV networks that combines GAN-based data augmentation, differential privacy, and machine learning classifiers to detect network attacks while preserving privacy and reducing bandwidth. To address severe class imbalance in the CIC-IDS2017 dataset, the authors generate synthetic minority-class network traffic samples and show substantial recall gains for underrepresented attack types after augmentation. CTGAN is run directly as the generator producing the synthetic intrusion samples that drive the entire data-augmentation and evaluation pipeline.

CTGAN is cited in the paper's survey and timeline of fine-grained traffic generators as one of several GAN-based prior methods situating the authors' own approach, but it is not run or benchmarked experimentally. CTGAN is only cited as related prior art in the survey/timeline, not executed.

Experiments on real VNF profiling datasets show FTCA reduces RMSE by 38.5% and improves R-squared by up to 68.6% over baseline regression. CTGAN is run directly as the core data-synthesis model whose generator is transferred between domains, forming the empirical backbone of the proposed FTCA pipeline.

The authors compare MCCE against several state-of-the-art on-manifold counterfactual methods across four datasets. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as an alternative generative method that could replace the decision trees in MCCE's first step, but it is not implemented or evaluated.

paper-syntheval-evaluation-framework-202.summary: Presents SynthEval, an evaluation framework for tabular synthetic data that treats utility and privacy as a panel of thirty metrics rather than a single score, handles mixed types without forcing an encoding, and lets users assemble and rank their own metric sets. SDV appears on both sides: SDMetrics is one of the four existing frameworks compared against, credited with quality and diagnostic reports but judged limited to high-level dataset similarity, and CTGAN is one of the four generators run through synthcity to produce the data the framework is demonstrated on.

paper-umap-smotenc-simple-efficient-2024.summary: This paper proposes UMAP-SMOTENC, a synthetic tabular data generation method combining a non-linear UMAP embedding with SMOTE-NC oversampling, aimed at balancing privacy protection and data utility more efficiently than deep generative alternatives. It is evaluated across eight datasets against several models and metrics, positioning itself as a lighter-weight substitute for costly deep-learning generators. TGAN is cited among the deep learning generative approaches the paper contrasts its method against as computationally expensive and unreliable for tabular data.
paper-umap-smotenc-simple-efficient-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was run as an experimental baseline (baseline_only) or only cited in related-work discussion (citation_only).

paper-comparative-analysis-gan-vae-2023.summary: This conference paper experimentally compares two deep-learning synthetic data generators, CTGAN (GAN-based) and TVAE (VAE-based), on two high-dimensional, highly imbalanced tabular datasets from Kaggle, finding that TVAE fails to generate minority-class samples when the minority class is very small. The experiments were run using Python 3.8.13 and the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) 0.17.1 library, which supplied both the CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers evaluated as the core generators of the entire empirical comparison.
paper-comparative-analysis-gan-vae-2023.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliations and industry framing inferred only from abstract/metadata, so precise domain application (if any) beyond generic tabular imbalance is unconfirmed.

paper-integrated-federated-learning-meta.summary: This conference paper proposes an architecture combining federated learning and meta-learning to optimize drill-and-blast design parameters across mines while keeping data local, tuning learning rate and boosting rounds to reduce RMSE by 28.6% over standard settings. To supplement scarce real mining data, the authors generate synthetic drill-and-blast datasets that preserve statistical properties from the literature. The SDV library is run directly to create these synthetic training/evaluation datasets, which are validated against domain experts and compared with a real-world benchmark dataset.
paper-integrated-federated-learning-meta.needs: Mining/drilling is not a listed industry category; mapped to energy_utilities as closest analog, though construction_infrastructure could also be argued.

paper-change-management-generative-model.summary: This paper proposes a framework for creating cloud-based "digital twins" of IT and IoT systems that serve as non-production environments for safely testing security patches and software updates, using generative AI models trained on small samples of real system data to synthesize varied testing scenarios. The work discusses conditional generator models for handling mixed attribute types in tabular data as motivation for its approach. TGAN and CTGAN are cited only in a background discussion of conditional generators for tabular data, with no evidence they were run.

paper-dptvae-driven-prior-tabular-2023.summary: This paper proposes DPTVAE, a new generative model for synthesizing tabular credit data that augments the variational autoencoder with a data-driven prior, evaluated presumably against existing tabular synthesizers on credit datasets. Only metadata and a citation link to the CTGAN/TVAE NeurIPS 2019 paper are available, with no abstract or full text obtained. The work appears to build directly on SDV's TVAE architecture, extending its generative prior for credit data synthesis.
paper-dptvae-driven-prior-tabular-2023.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether DPTVAE reimplements TVAE from scratch (port), extends SDV's own ctgan-package TVAE code (derivative_work), or merely cites it. Integration marked unclear pending full text.

paper-privacy-metaverse-ecosystem-2023.summary: A book chapter surveying data privacy challenges in the metaverse, introducing privacy regulations and privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) such as anonymization, encryption, and synthetic data generation across the data lifecycle. It offers educational guidance for readers on adopting existing privacy-preserving techniques for metaverse applications rather than proposing new methods. The chapter cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper as an example of synthetic data generation technology relevant to privacy protection.
paper-privacy-metaverse-ecosystem-2023.needs: No full text or citing sentence was available; placement of SDV within the PET discussion is inferred only from the abstract and citation record.

paper-defect-identification-method-ultra.summary: This paper proposes a zero-shot learning framework, Feature-GAN-ZSL, that fuses ultrasonic inspection signal features with expert-defined semantic descriptions to detect unseen classes of pipeline weld defects (incomplete fusion, slag entrapment) when labeled samples are scarce, using a GAN to synthesize unseen-class features and a classifier to sharpen discrimination. The evidence shows the CTGAN and vine-copula papers are cited in sentences discussing an unrelated feature extractor and semantic word-vector embeddings, with no apparent engagement with either SDV method's actual technique.
paper-defect-identification-method-ultra.needs: Citing sentences for both SDV papers describe unrelated content (a feature extractor tree, semantic word vectors), suggesting mis-citation or reference-numbering mismatch rather than genuine use of CTGAN or vine copulas; full text needed to confirm.

paper-enhanced-explainable-deep-learning.summary: This MILCOM paper proposes an IoT intrusion detection framework that combines CTGAN-based dataset expansion for minority attack classes, Boruta SHAP feature selection, and SHAP-based explainability, validated on the NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 datasets. The authors describe CTGAN's conditional generator and mode-specific normalization and use it to synthesize thousands of additional minority-class network traffic rows, showing large AUC gains for rare attack types after augmentation. CTGAN is run as the core data-augmentation generator underpinning the whole empirical pipeline, targeting minority attack classes via its conditional generation mechanism.
paper-enhanced-explainable-deep-learning.needs: Not fully clear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package specifically was used versus another CTGAN implementation, though no reimplementation details are given, suggesting library use.

paper-improving-stock-market-intraday-20.summary: This paper proposes a framework for improving intraday stock price forecasting by training an LSTM predictor on a mix of real and synthetic data, where the synthetic data is generated by a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) incorporating a mode-normalization procedure to stabilize training. The framework is evaluated on real stock data with quantitative and qualitative criteria, showing improved forecasting accuracy over using real data alone. The mode-normalization technique is adapted from CTGAN's mode-specific normalization concept, cited but not run as the library itself -- the authors build their own WGAN-GP generator rather than using SDV's CTGAN.
paper-improving-stock-market-intraday-20.needs: The full-text extraction found no direct SDV-family mention; the CTGAN citation is inferred from metadata only, so the exact wording of the citation sentence is unverified.

paper-maize-yield-prediction-federated-2.summary: This paper proposes a federated learning approach for maize yield prediction using a random forest model trained across distributed agricultural data sources without centralizing raw data. It addresses privacy and data-sharing constraints common in agricultural datasets while aiming to maintain prediction accuracy comparable to centralized training. The evidence gives no citing sentence or full text, only that CTGAN's NeurIPS 2019 paper is cited, with no indication of how or whether it was run.
paper-maize-yield-prediction-federated-2.needs: No full text or citing sentence available; cannot determine whether CTGAN was run, used for data augmentation, or merely cited in passing.

paper-global-measure-simultaneously-eval.summary: This paper proposes DUPI, a new global measure that simultaneously evaluates data utility and privacy risk in synthetic or de-identified datasets, along with a graphical tool visualizing the utility-privacy trade-off, and shows it outperforms existing utility-only measures like PSM and CAM on simulated and real datasets. To test the measure empirically, the authors generate synthetic versions of real datasets (German, Bank, Wine) using three synthesis techniques -- a CART-based algorithm (synthpop), TGAN, and CTABGAN -- and compare DUPI results across them. TGAN, the SDV-family precursor to CTGAN, is run as one of three synthetic data generators whose output is evaluated by the proposed metric.
paper-global-measure-simultaneously-eval.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was run via the original sdv-dev TGAN package or a reimplementation, nor the extent of its role in the empirical results beyond the abstract-context citing sentence.

paper-open-case-reasoning-framework-2022.summary: Proposes a case-based reasoning (CBR) framework for personalized on-board driving assistance in traffic risk scenarios, introducing an FFMTE model to model traffic events from the 100-Car Naturalistic Driving Study dataset and a tailored CBR pipeline to recommend evasive maneuvers and cushion times. To address class imbalance between crash/near-crash and normal events, the authors build a CTGAN-augmented dataset alongside SMOTE and random-oversampling variants and compare downstream FFMTE performance across them. CTGAN, run directly via the SDV library (linked to sdv.dev's single-table CTGAN user guide), is used as one of three data-augmentation methods evaluated, with SMOTE ultimately outperforming it.

paper-disparate-membership-inference-202.summary: Studies why membership inference attacks succeed unevenly across the class-based subsets of a dataset rather than uniformly, and tests whether the disparity can be engineered away by hardening the data itself, through feature reduction based on correlation thresholds or on manifold structure and through class balancing by oversampling or undersampling. CTGAN is the oversampler: it was chosen over ADASYN and SMOTE because those rely on linear connections between observations while CTGAN learns the distribution of the subset being sampled, and the combination of manifold-based feature reduction with CTGAN oversampling is the best-performing treatment, cutting disparate attack accuracy while leaving victim model performance effectively unchanged. SDV's generator is thus run as one experimental treatment inside a study about attack vulnerability rather than as the paper's subject.

paper-contribution-synthetic-generation-.summary: A review examining how synthetic tabular data generation methods could help address data sparsity and scarcity in palliative care research, surveying GAN- and VAE-based approaches for generating patient records and discussing perspectives for their use in palliative screening. The review describes CTGAN and TGAN among a broader survey of tabular GAN architectures in its narrative background section, without running any of them experimentally. CTGAN's conditional GAN architecture with conditional vectors for categorical values is cited and described as prior art, but not implemented or benchmarked.

paper-exome-ensemble-cancer-2022.summary: Classifies cancer type from whole-exome variant data with an ensemble of standard learners, and confronts a sample size too small for the feature count by augmenting the exome table with synthetic records before training, reporting classifier accuracy before and after. Both generators are Xu et al.'s: CTGAN is run for 300 epochs at batch size 10 with the reported generator and discriminator losses, and TVAE alongside it, with the paper reproducing CTGAN's conditional generator and discriminator equations to explain what it ran.

paper-incorporation-synthetic-generation.summary: This paper presents the VITALISE project's controlled data-processing workflow, which lets researchers upload Living Lab health and wellbeing data, generate synthetic versions locally, develop analyses on the synthetic data, and then execute the validated analysis remotely on the real data to preserve privacy and comply with data protection laws. The authors implement and evaluate this workflow using heart-rate time-series and tabular assets from Living Labs. The SDV library's Probabilistic AutoRegressive (PAR) model is run as the synthetic-data generator for the time-series asset, and SDV's tabular data model is also tried but found less representative, making SDV the operational engine behind the whole empirical evaluation.

paper-ctgan-tgan-which-one-2021.summary: This work empirically compares two GAN-based tabular synthesizers, TGAN and CTGAN, to determine which better generates synthetic EEG signal data, showing sample outputs from each model. The comparison is framed as a direct evaluation of generator quality for a biomedical time-series/tabular use case. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of the two generators being compared against TGAN.
paper-ctgan-tgan-which-one-2021.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliation inferred from the Hanyang University publication portal URL, not from explicit text. Cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented.

paper-comment-gmd-2020-427-2021.summary: This is a peer-review comment (open review) on a manuscript describing a copula-based approach to synthetically augmenting training data for a neural-network emulator of downwelling longwave radiation in a weather/climate context, reporting large reductions in mean absolute error from copula-augmented datasets. The comment engages with that manuscript's methodology and cites the original SDV paper in discussing the copula-based data-generation approach. SDV is referenced as background for the copula-modeling method the reviewed work builds on, not run or benchmarked within the comment itself.
paper-comment-gmd-2020-427-2021.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether this review comment or the manuscript it discusses actually runs SDV software versus citing it for methodological context, and which party (reviewer vs. author) the SDV citation belongs to.

paper-curl-coupled-representation-learni.summary: This paper proposes CuRL and tCuRL, coupled representation learning methods that generate session-based interaction pairs from a bipartite card-merchant transaction graph and feed them to a skip-gram model to learn joint embeddings for fraud detection. The authors show these embeddings outperform graph-based and random-walk baselines while being faster to compute. To validate that a released/compared synthetic version of their transaction dataset matches the real one at an aggregate level, they run SDV's Evaluation Framework, reporting Chi-squared and Kolmogorov-Smirnov test scores.
paper-curl-coupled-representation-learni.needs: Not fully clear whether the synthetic dataset being evaluated was itself generated with SDV or by another method; only the evaluation framework's use is confirmed.

paper-deep-learning-generate-synthetic-2.summary: This paper proposes a deep-learning framework to generate synthetic tabular behavioral data from a small cognitive-psychology Stroop-task dataset (N=102), addressing the shortage of sample size for downstream analysis. It fine-tunes a pre-trained conditional GAN model for tabular data and introduces five statistical evaluation methods to compare generated data against the original at instance, feature, and whole-set levels. The synthetic data are produced using a pre-trained CTGAN model, whose hyperparameters (Table 2) are reported and reused as the core generator underlying the entire empirical framework.
paper-deep-learning-generate-synthetic-2.needs: Full parameter table (embedding_dim, generator_dim, etc.) not shown in evidence excerpt, but strongly implied given reference to 'pre-trained ct-gan model' and CTGAN citation.

paper-growing-synthetic-differentially-p.summary: This paper proposes COPULA-SHIRLEY, a differentially-private synthetic data generation method based on vine copulas, and evaluates its utility and privacy protection (via a membership inference attack) on real datasets. The work situates itself among recent advances in vine copula construction, citing prior methods that use Lasso and reinforcement learning with LSTMs for near-optimal vine selection. One of the SDV-family vine copula papers is cited only as related work on vine copula construction techniques, not run or extended in the experiments described.
paper-growing-synthetic-differentially-p.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether the SDV vine-copula paper is discussed further in related work or only cited in this one sentence.

paper-hyperspectral-image-classification.summary: This is a review paper surveying deep-learning methods for hyperspectral image (HSI) classification under conditions of insufficient labeled training data, covering feature-learning strategies and benchmarking results across popular HSI datasets. It discusses synthetic and simulated data generation as one strategy to overcome data scarcity, citing prior work showing synthetic datasets can improve or even outperform photorealistic training data. The SDV paper (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only in passing, alongside another synthetic-data reference, to support this general claim about synthetic data's value, with no SDV code run or algorithm engaged.
paper-hyperspectral-image-classification.needs: Only abstract and citing sentences available; full text not obtained, so cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in the body beyond this generic citation.

paper-relational-synthesis-generative-ad.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive experimental study of GAN-based relational data synthesis, introducing a unified framework that decomposes prior GAN approaches (including TGAN and CTGAN) into design choices such as data transformation, network architecture, and training strategy, then benchmarking combinations of these choices. It finds that GMM-based normalization outperforms simple normalization for multi-modal numerical attributes and offers guidance on selecting design solutions. TGAN's and CTGAN's mode-specific (GMM) normalization and sequence-generation ideas are discussed and reimplemented as design components within the authors' own framework, while the Synthetic Data Vault's copula-based approach is cited only in passing as related work; no SDV-family code is run.

paper-analytics-privacy-concerned-world-.summary: A conceptual marketing-research paper that maps functions of data analytics and privacy (collection, storage, verification, analytics, dissemination) across consumer, intermediary, and firm levels, and assesses how well various analytics methods protect consumer privacy. It surveys prospective techniques including differential privacy and generative approaches without running experiments. SDV's multivariate Gaussian copula approach is cited in passing as an example of promising privacy-preserving data synthesis research, with no implementation or evaluation.

preprint-orthogonal-procrustes-problem-p.summary: This preprint proposes a lightweight postprocessing method for synthetic tabular data that uses the Orthogonal Procrustes problem to restore the Pearson correlation structure of an original dataset while largely preserving feature distributions and downstream classification performance. The authors test their correction step on synthetic samples produced by five generation methods (SMOTE, ADASYN, Gaussian Copula, TVAE, and CTGAN) across several datasets including a credit-card fraud dataset. SDV's Gaussian Copula and TVAE synthesizers, and CTGAN, are run as three of the five generators whose outputs are corrected and evaluated, serving as evaluation subjects rather than baselines the authors reject or a model they modify.
preprint-orthogonal-procrustes-problem-p.needs: Affiliation list has 4 authors but only 3 distinct organizations (Karlstad University appears twice); affiliation_types/countries arrays given per distinct org as required.

preprint-samplellm-optimizing-tabular-sy.summary: This preprint proposes SampleLLM, a two-stage LLM-based framework for synthesizing tabular data for recommendation tasks, combining Chain-of-Thought prompted exemplar generation with a feature-attribution-based importance sampling refinement step. The authors benchmark against numerous tabular synthesis baselines (CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM, GReaT, REaLTabFormer, etc.) and evaluate synthetic data fidelity throughout via an 'SDV similarity' score based on column shapes and pair trends. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is cited as foundational prior work in tabular synthesis, and its similarity/quality metric is repeatedly run to score synthetic outputs against the original data.
preprint-samplellm-optimizing-tabular-sy.needs: The 'SDV similarity' metric (column shapes + pair trends) matches SDMetrics functionality but is attributed by the authors to the original SDV paper [45]; recorded per the paper's own citation rather than corrected.

preprint-enhancing-network-intrusion-det.summary: This paper proposes augmenting network intrusion detection system (NIDS) training data with synthetic attack traffic generated by three GAN variants -- Vanilla GAN, WGAN, and Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) -- to counter data scarcity and class imbalance in the CIC-IDS2017 dataset, evaluating fidelity via cosine similarity and cumulative feature sums and downstream IDS classifier performance. CTGAN underperformed the other two generators in both similarity and IDS enhancement metrics in their experiments. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of three generators producing synthetic minority-class (Botnet) samples for data augmentation, compared against Vanilla GAN and WGAN.
preprint-enhancing-network-intrusion-det.needs: No explicit mention of the sdv-dev CTGAN package, constructor parameters, or an authors' own reimplementation is given, so whether the library itself was run or reimplemented cannot be confirmed from the evidence.

preprint-large-language-models-llms-2024.summary: A survey published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research that consolidates recent research applying large language models to tabular data tasks -- prediction, data synthesis/augmentation, and table understanding -- reviewing datasets, metrics, and methodologies. It situates LLM-based approaches against traditional and deep-learning synthetic data methods, positioning Copula-based and GAN-based generators as prior art before the modern generative-model era. SDV's original Copula-based synthesizer and CTGAN are each cited once as examples of these traditional and deep-learning tabular data generation approaches, without being run or evaluated.

preprint-black-box-training-identificati.summary: This paper studies membership inference attacks against GANs in a black-box setting, where the adversary has only sample access to the generator rather than the discriminator. The authors introduce 'The Detector', a second network trained to distinguish GAN-generated samples from real ones, and evaluate it on image GANs (CIFAR10) and tabular GANs trained on genomic data. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GANs used for tabular data generation, with no experiment run on it.

preprint-evaluation-key-survey-evaluatio.summary: A survey that catalogues and analyzes measures for evaluating synthetic time-series data, arguing that no consensus exists on evaluation procedures and providing a guide to help researchers select appropriate metrics. It does not propose a new generative model but surveys the evaluation landscape across generative approaches for time series. The SDV-family paper on sequential models (PAR/DeepEcho) appears only in the reference list, with no discussion or engagement in the body text.

preprint-infrastructure-synthetic-health.summary: A BioHackathon Europe 2022 project report proposing a containerised infrastructure for generating and FAIR-sharing synthetic health data, prototyped on a breast-cancer clinical dataset and compared across three generators (SDV, DataSynthesizer, SyntheaTM). The authors run SDV directly, comparing its GaussianCopula and CTGAN parameterizations, using its relational/table-metadata modelling approach, and evaluating outputs with the SDMetrics library and a downstream classification task. SDV's Synthetic Data Vault framework -- its GaussianCopula and CTGAN synthesizers plus SDMetrics evaluation -- is run as the core generator and evaluation tool underlying the project's proof of concept.
preprint-infrastructure-synthetic-health.needs: Affiliation department-level detail was collapsed to institution names per instructions; BSC and EMBL-EBI classified as nonprofit research institutes rather than academic, which is a judgment call.

preprint-pytrial-machine-learning-softwa.summary: PyTrial is an open-source Python benchmark platform implementing 34 machine learning algorithms across six clinical trial tasks -- including patient outcome prediction, trial site selection, and synthetic patient data simulation -- along with 23 curated ML-ready datasets and a unified four-step API for data loading, model specification, training, and evaluation. For the patient tabular data simulation task, PyTrial wraps GaussianCopula, CopulaGAN, TVAE, and CTGAN as interchangeable synthesizers alongside MedGAN and RNNGAN. SDV's GaussianCopula, CopulaGAN, and TVAE models are integrated as several of multiple interchangeable generators offered for the platform's patient simulation benchmark task.
preprint-pytrial-machine-learning-softwa.needs: Whether CTGAN was invoked via the sdv package's wrapper or the standalone ctgan library is not explicit, though the shared module naming with CopulaGAN (SDV-exclusive) suggests the sdv package.

preprint-reimagining-synthetic-tabular-g.summary: This NeurIPS 2023 paper introduces a data-centric AI framework for evaluating and improving synthetic tabular data generation, showing that data profiling metrics (e.g. identifying easy/ambiguous/hard samples) better predict downstream utility than standard statistical fidelity metrics. The authors benchmark five state-of-the-art generative models across eleven tabular datasets and propose practical guidance on model and feature selection informed by data profiles. CTGAN and TVAE, obtained via the synthcity library's implementations, are run as two of the five generative models in this benchmark, with CTGAN cited to the original SDV-family paper.
preprint-reimagining-synthetic-tabular-g.needs: CTGAN/TVAE were obtained through the synthcity toolkit's implementation rather than a direct sdv-dev import, so the code lineage to SDV is indirect (inherited) rather than a direct api_user call.

paper-transcoralnet-credit-2023.summary: Attacks the cold-start problem in supply-chain credit assessment, where a new industry has no labelled default history, with a two-stream transformer whose shared-weight encoders take source-industry records in one stream and target-industry records in the other, aligned by a CORAL domain-adaptation loss and explained through LIME. CTGAN supplies the target stream: it is trained to model the target-domain feature distribution and the synthetic records it produces are what the lower stream consumes, so the cold-start result depends on it.

preprint-differentially-private-syntheti.summary: This paper proposes ε-PrivateSMOTE, a privacy-preserving technique that combines SMOTE-style noise-induced interpolation with differential privacy to selectively obfuscate high-risk records for re-identification, aiming to improve the privacy-utility-efficiency trade-off over existing synthesizers. The authors benchmark it against traditional and deep-learning privacy techniques, including generative adversarial networks and variational autoencoders, and use SDMetrics for utility evaluation. The SDV library is run to generate CopulaGAN, TVAE, and CTGAN synthetic data variants as baseline comparators, and SDV's SDMetrics is used to compute data utility scores.
